note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one City of Albuquerque page: the pickleball page, whose "Pickleball Court Locations" table gives every venue a name, an address and a description cell that states the kind of court and the count, and whose prose beneath the table states hours for the two complexes, the first come, first served rule with its ninety-minute limit, the Sierra Vista phone reservation and the lesson programme. The county and the postcode come from the US Census address geocoder. The City writes most addresses without a street type and the Census supplied one; every published address matched at house-number level without a second resolver. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Thirty-three pickleball courts, twenty-one of them lit, at the City of Albuquerque's principal pickleball complex in the south-east of the city. The City's table cell reads "Pickleball Complex / 33 Courts (21 Lighted)", and its prose names this as the first of the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes", so these are pickleball courts rather than tennis courts carrying a second set of lines.

Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex's thirty-three is the largest single-venue count on this site. The number is new to the record: the City's page source still holds "18 Courts (6 Lighted)" inside a comment no browser renders, and the visible table is what publishes.

This is also where the City teaches the game. Its 2026 lessons, Junior Basics, Adult Basics and Intermediate Play, "will take place at Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex", with classes "limited to six participants" and registration at play.cabq.gov or through the Jerry Cline Tennis Facility, 505-224-6682.
slots.getting_there:
501 Elizabeth SE, Albuquerque, NM 87123. The City writes the address without a street type, and the US Census address geocoder matched it as "501 ELIZABETH ST SE" at house-number level, in Bernalillo County inside the incorporated place Albuquerque. The postcode is the resolver's, since the City's visible table prints none.

The City publishes nothing about parking at the complex and nothing about restrooms. It does publish two phone numbers: the reservations line, 505-224-6682, and the City Pickleball Manager, 505-224-6693.
slots.what_to_expect:
Open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, in the City's sentence "Manzano Mesa, Villella, and Pat Hurley are open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily." With twenty-one lit courts the evening end of that window is usable. The other twelve courts carry no lighting statement.

Play is "on a first come, first serve basis" and "limited to 1.5 hours when others are waiting". Thirty-three courts is a scale at which turning up alone and finding a game is a reasonable plan, though the City publishes no open-play time. The complex can be reserved for tournaments through the City's Sports Office. Price, surface, nets and indoor or outdoor are not stated.

faqs.a: Twenty-one of the thirty-three are, on the City's cell. The other twelve carry no lighting statement either way, so they are recorded as not stated.
Not stated. The City publishes no price for any pickleball court in Albuquerque, and a court is not recorded as free unless the operator says so.

slots.description:

The table cell reads "Pickleball Complex / 6 Courts", and the prose beneath it names "Villella Pickleball Courts" as the second of the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes", spelling the name with a double l where the table has one. The table's spelling, Villela, is the one used here.

A dedicated court is a pickleball court whenever you arrive, with nothing to share and nothing to set up. In Albuquerque that puts Villela in a group of two with Manzano Mesa, against nine parks where the count is a count of lines on tennis courts. Six courts is enough for a rotation rather than a single game.

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts of two kinds at a City tennis complex in the north-west. The table reads "Tennis/Pickleball Courts / 2 Courts and 4 Lined Courts", and the prose says the same thing in longer words: one of "two shared complexes at Sierra Vista Courts with 2 permanent pickleball courts, and 4 lined pickleball courts". Two courts stand as pickleball courts; four are lines on tennis courts. The distinction matters on arrival, because two of the six are certain and four depend on what the tennis courts are being used for.

This is the one Albuquerque venue whose courts the City says can be booked: "Courts at Sierra Vista can be reserved in advanced by calling 505-767-5445." That number is the complex's own, distinct from the Sports Office line for tournaments and special events. The City states no price for a reservation.

Without a booking the rule is the City's general one: "first come, first serve", ninety minutes when others are waiting. With a booking, made by phone, a court is yours for the time agreed at a price the City does not state. Hours are not stated: the City's 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. sentence names Manzano Mesa, Villella and Pat Hurley, not Sierra Vista. Lighting, price, surface, nets and indoor or outdoor are not stated.

Two courts is a game rather than a rotation. A four can play; an eight will wait. Hoffman is one of nine Albuquerque parks the City writes this way, and one of two, with Rinconada Park, at the smallest count. The table states the count and the address and nothing else about the place: no hours, no lighting, no description of the park around the courts.

A tennis court with pickleball lines is a tennis court first; the pickleball count is the number of pickleball courts marked on it, and the tennis net is the net that is there.
